note: Cures the upstream pattern fork has no module for. Own-authored, so the detector and the specimen it points at ship from one commit and cannot drift apart — which is why this source carries no pinned commit. `count` is not decoration: the shared seeder refuses to sweep rows this file no longer claims unless the claimed rows equal it, so a truncated read cannot be mistaken for a deletion. Keep it equal to the length of `samples`.

samples.principle: Compose Method: reshape a long method into a short sequence of intention-revealing calls, each at one level of abstraction below the caller.
samples.situation: when one method interleaves several jobs at different levels of abstraction, so a reader must hold parsing, arithmetic and formatting in mind at once
samples.cause: the jobs share a scope, so a change to any one of them is made in the presence of all the others and can only be verified by reading the whole method
samples.details:
BEFORE: org.jawata.samples/compose-method/src/main/java/org/jawata/samples/composemethod/OrderReportBefore.java — one method selects, totals, formats and renders, with loop bodies at the same indentation as the policy decisions.
AFTER: org.jawata.samples/compose-method/src/main/java/org/jawata/samples/composemethod/OrderReportAfter.java — the entry point reads as its own intention; parsing is a function of a line, totalling of the parsed items, rendering of the totals.
COST: five members where there was one, and a reader chasing a detail follows a call instead of scrolling. Worth it when the jobs change at different times; not worth it for a long method that does exactly one thing.
symptoms: one method mixes parsing, calculation and formatting
the reader must scroll to find where one job ends and the next begins

samples.principle: Replace Pattern with Idiom: when the language absorbs a pattern, keep the design and drop the ceremony — a single-method interface with anonymous implementations is a lambda spelled the long way.
samples.situation: when a strategy or callback is expressed as anonymous classes implementing a single-method interface, and the ceremony is longer than the behaviour it wraps
samples.cause: the pattern was written when the language had no way to express it, and the boilerplate now hides the one expression that distinguishes each implementation
samples.details:
BEFORE: org.jawata.samples/replace-pattern-with-idiom/src/main/java/org/jawata/samples/replacepatternwithidiom/RetryPolicyBefore.java — three backoff policies, each five lines of ceremony around one expression, plus a Supplier written as an anonymous class.
AFTER: org.jawata.samples/replace-pattern-with-idiom/src/main/java/org/jawata/samples/replacepatternwithidiom/RetryPolicyAfter.java — lambdas for the trivial policies, a method reference where the rationale deserves a name and a doc comment, and @FunctionalInterface so the compiler defends the single-method property.
COST: a lambda has no name and nowhere to hang a doc comment. The transformation refuses a strategy that carries state or implements more than one method — those keep their class.
symptoms: anonymous classes implementing a one-method interface
a Supplier or Runnable written as a class body
